subject: Re: MAP & perf checkpoints — Hightide performance + variant plan
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@hightide.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Brovkin <elena@hightide.ai>; procurement@hightide.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: performance checkpoints & variant tradeoffs

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Hightide is keen to move to a short MAP focusing on response-time SLAs for our triage assistant (goal: sub-200ms median TTFT, sustain 30 concurrent inference sessions at peak) and a decision on the model variant to ship. Procurement also wants a clear close timeline and the perf evidence to include latency/TTFT, throughput, and concurrency behavior.

Can Redwood own a short benchmarking plan and share results we can review with engineering and procurement next week? We prefer results on our sample prompts (attached test set) and a short summary that calls out quality vs perf tradeoffs across variants in your catalog.

Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Product, Hightide Health

----
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Tom Harris <tharris@hightide.ai>
Cc: Elena Brovkin <elena@hightide.ai>, ava_chen@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: performance checkpoints & variant tradeoffs

Tom —

Appreciate the quick follow up. We can own the MAP and deliver an evidence pack by Friday (summary + raw CSV + brief variant recommendation). High-level plan below; I’ll drop a MAP workbook to the Drive (see link) and loop in procurement contacts for the close timeline.

MAP high-level items (owner — target):
- Test harness & infra snapshot (Dev — Dev Patel) — Thu EOD 2026-04-09
- Baseline runs: latency/TTFT/throughput at 1,5,15,30 concurrency (Dev) — Fri 2026-04-10 morning
- Quality smoke: 200 prompt sample comparison across 3 variants (Ava) — Fri 2026-04-10 afternoon
- Results pack & recommendation (Sean) — Fri 2026-04-10 EOD
- Procurement ready summary + PO terms (Marissa) — Mon 2026-04-13

Acceptance criteria we propose:
- Median TTFT <= 200ms on chosen variant at 10 concurrent sessions for standard prompt mix
- 95th pct latency degradation no more than 2.5x from median under 30 concurrency
- Human-checked quality delta <= 4 points (A/B rubric) between chosen variant and baseline high-quality model

Deliverables:
- CSV with per-request timestamps and metrics (attached as benchmark_results_2026-04-10.csv)
- One-page model comparison (model_comparison_summary.pdf)
- MAP workbook with milestones and owners (Hightide_MAP_v3.xlsx)

I’ll coordinate the runs in us-west-2 infra to match your production region. If that works I’ll proceed and we’ll schedule a 30-min review on Monday (2026-04-13).

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai; ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@hightide.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: performance checkpoints & variant tradeoffs

Quick tech note on the harness and models we’ll exercise:

Test harness:
- Workload driver: adjusted to replay Hightide sample set with 95th/uniform timing profiles
- Measurement: TTFT (server send-first-byte) and per-token steady-state latency; end-to-end wall-clock for whole response
- Env: dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool (g5.48xlarge-equivalent), pinned model kernels, no tenant multiplexing

Model variants to test (initial):
- Variant A: redwood/rdw-13b-v2 (fp16, baseline high-quality)
- Variant B: redwood/rdw-7b-qat (quantized fast-path — lower memory, lower perf in long context)
- Variant C: open-melody-13b-8bit (community variant we’ve verified, lower cost)

Test matrix:
- Sequence lengths: 32, 128, 512 (representing quick replies, multi-turn, long messages)
- Concurrency: 1, 5, 15, 30 sessions (sustained for 10 minutes each)
- Metrics: median TTFT, 95th TTFT, tokens/sec, percent requests exceeding 1s

I’ll attach the harness config and will seed runs early Friday. Note: caching enabled for repeated prefixes unless Hightide requests cold-cache only runs.

— Dev
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: harness_config_v2.yaml (stub)

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Tom Harris <tharris@hightide.ai>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: performance checkpoints & variant tradeoffs

Tom —

We ran the planned matrix this morning and validated the sample prompts. Short summary of what we checked for quality:
- Quality rubric: relevance (0-5), correctness (0-5), safety flags (binary), fluency (0-5) — human annotations on 200 prompts across variants
- A/B sampling: blind comparison between Variant A and B, and A and C

I’ll compile the human scores into the summary PDF. Dev attached raw timings CSV. Two notes:
1) Variant B consistently hit sub-200ms median TTFT at short sequences (32 tokens) and at 10 concurrent sessions, but under 512 tokens the effective tokens/sec drops ~22% compared to Variant A.
2) Variant C has the lowest cost but shows a quality delta of ~6 points average vs Variant A on our rubric (quality loss concentrated in medical-safety rewrites).

Next steps per MAP: Sean to present recommendation + Marissa to finalize procurement terms.

Ava Chen
Product — Evaluation & Evals, Redwood Inference

Attachment: benchmark_results_2026-04-10.csv (stub)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Tom Harris <tharris@hightide.ai>; Elena Brovkin <elena@hightide.ai>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai; dev_patel@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; procurement@hightide.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: performance checkpoints & variant tradeoffs

Team —

Attached is the results pack (model_comparison_summary.pdf) and the raw CSV. TL;DR recommendation:
- Choose Variant B (redwood/rdw-7b-qat) for initial rollout if Hightide prioritizes unit-cost and TTFT at short contexts. Variant B meets median TTFT <= 200ms at 10 concurrent sessions for 32-token responses and sustains ~30 concurrent sessions with median TTFT ~240ms.
- If Hightide requires stronger safety/medical correctness for longer contexts (512 tokens), Variant A (rdw-13b-v2) is the recommended baseline — expect ~18–25% higher per-token cost and ~20% higher latency in long-context tails.

Acceptance criteria review (status):
- Median TTFT <= 200ms at 10 concurrent: achieved on Variant B for short sequences (PASS)
- 95th pct latency degradation <= 2.5x at 30 concurrency: Variant B measured at ~2.1x (PASS)
- Quality delta <= 4 points vs baseline: Variant B delta = 3.8 (PASS), Variant C delta = 6.2 (FAIL)

Proposed close timeline:
- Decision on variant: 2026-04-14 (Thu) 
- Procurement signature + PO submitted: 2026-04-20 (Tue)
- Initial rollout (canary): 2026-05-01

Requested next step: Tom/Elena — confirm that Variant B is acceptable for pilot (I’ll update the MAP workbook and Marissa will draft the PO summary). I’ll include cost projections for both Variant A and B in the procurement brief.

Attachments: model_comparison_summary.pdf; benchmark_results_2026-04-10.csv; Hightide_MAP_v3.xlsx

Thanks —
Sean

----
From: Elena Brovkin <elena@hightide.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@hightide.ai>; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; procurement@hightide.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: performance checkpoints & variant tradeoffs

Sean —

Thanks for the thorough pack. We reviewed the model_comparison_summary with engineering and procurement. Initial acceptance: proceed with Variant B for pilot under the following constraints:
- Scope: 0.5M tokens/month for pilot, 3-month performance review
- Audit: Redwood to provide detailed per-request traces for any incidents during pilot (redacted PII)
- Escalation: automatic fallback to Variant A on safety-critical prompts (we’ll share a small seed list)

We can target decision confirmation 2026-04-14 and procurement signature by 2026-04-20 as proposed. Please send the PO summary and final MAP workbook when ready — procurement is on copy.

— Elena
VP Engineering, Hightide Health
